core_claim.quote: Activity in internal representations does not generate the experience of seeing. The outside world serves as its own, external, representation.

source.citation: O'Regan JK, Noë A. A sensorimotor account of vision and visual consciousness. Behavioral and Brain Sciences 24(5):939-973 (target article), with open peer commentary and the authors' response, 973-1031, 2001

prediction.statement: Because the brain keeps no detailed picture of the scene, large changes made in full view go unnoticed when the brief flicker of motion that would normally draw attention to them is masked (by a blank flash, an eye movement, a blink, a film cut or scattered 'mud splashes'), even when the person is looking straight at the place that changes.

first_stated.passage: The idea that the world constitutes an outside memory, and that we only see what we are currently attending to, was the impetus for a number of surprising experiments performed recently on “change blindness”

source.citation: O'Regan JK, Noë A. A sensorimotor account of vision and visual consciousness. Behavioral and Brain Sciences 24(5):939-973 (target article), with open peer commentary and the authors' response, 973-1031, 2001

prediction.test_for: When the local signal of a change is masked, people often take many repetitions to find, or fail to find, large changes in natural scenes, including on occasions when eye tracking shows they were looking at the changing spot when it changed.
prediction.test_against: When the local signal is masked, people find large changes about as quickly and reliably as when it is not masked.
